assertion_audit.failure_condition: Changing the submission partition, removing --wait or retaining scheduler environment variables fails the recording-scheduler assertions.
Withholding either composed prompt call fails len(calls)==2; observed in negative-control.log.

CLI failure, wrong base/head forwarding, invalid observation fields, missing completion, wrong partition, missing revision/command header or missing exit receipt fails the corresponding assertion; identities are independently read from pointer and git HEAD, and scheduler argv is checked separately.
A wrapper .sh or .py created beside the actual dispatch prompt fails the no-script checks; the prompt is a positive control for the directory being examined.
Manifest audit rejection, suite delta rejection or fewer/more than three scheduler submissions fails these assertions.

Resolving both commands against the same revision includes the added test in baseline or excludes it from head; a copied baseline test population also breaks the independent one/two-pass log expectations.
Swallowing command exit 7, marking it successful, losing the executed marker or losing EXIT=7 fails these checks.
Removing checkout ownership validation allows submission or loses the refusal text and fails these checks.
Treating a successful submission with no job receipt as a completed gate fails the nonzero-exit and completed-false assertions.
Removing worker/arm help or partition support, or adding a caller log option, fails help checks; accepting --log-path also fails its explicit usage refusal.

assertion_independence: No vacuous comparison of a supplied value to its returned copy was counted as regression coverage: header comparisons measure serialization, independent pointer/git identities constrain revision labels, and recording-scheduler argv checks constrain the reported partition. Fixture assert True statements only seed the measured population.
